package_info.package_versions: 2022 version 17.3 and earlier; 2021 version 16.4.2 and earlier
package_info.why_malicious: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in the QuarkXPress Drawing (QXD) file decoding plugin allow attackers to execute arbitrary code or leak sensitive information by supplying specially crafted QXD files. These vulnerabilities enable exploitation through malformed input, violating user and system security expectations.

execution_context.file_location: QXD file parsing plugin (internal InDesign code, not user-accessible)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (qxd_data_length > buffer_size) { buffer[qxd_data_length] = value; } // improper bounds check, leads to out-of-bounds write
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, based on Adobe plugin development)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted QXD file is opened, the code fails to properly check bounds before writing to a buffer, allowing out-of-bounds memory writes, which can result in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Out-of-bounds writes are a classic vector for arbitrary code execution, especially when triggered by untrusted file input.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal file parsing should strictly validate all input sizes and never write outside allocated buffers. Here, the code allows unchecked writes based on attacker-controlled data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Buffer manipulation is common in file parsing, but always with strict bounds checks.
key_indicators: Improper bounds check on attacker-controlled data
Triggered by opening a crafted file

execution_context.file_location: QXD file parsing plugin (internal InDesign code, not user-accessible)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: value = buffer[qxd_data_length]; // improper bounds check, leads to out-of-bounds read
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, based on Adobe plugin development)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted QXD file is opened, the code fails to properly check bounds before reading from a buffer, allowing out-of-bounds memory reads, which can result in sensitive information disclosure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Out-of-bounds reads can leak sensitive memory contents, including user data or application secrets, especially when triggered by attacker-supplied files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal file parsing should never read outside allocated buffers. Here, the code allows unchecked reads based on attacker-controlled data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Buffer reads are common, but always with strict bounds checks.
key_indicators: Improper bounds check on attacker-controlled data
Triggered by opening a crafted file

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious QXD file with malformed data designed to trigger out-of-bounds memory access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the malicious file in Adobe InDesign.

attack_chain.action: Victim opens the crafted QXD file in Adobe InDesign, triggering the vulnerable plugin code.
Out-of-bounds write (snippet_1) enables arbitrary code execution, or out-of-bounds read (snippet_2) leaks sensitive memory contents.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution or sensitive information disclosure within the context of the application.

behavioral_signatures: Opening QXD files results in unexpected memory access violations (crashes, exceptions)
Unusual process behavior or crashes when handling QXD files
Execution of code or shellcode after opening a QXD file
file_indicators: QXD files with malformed or oversized data fields
QXD files that cause InDesign to crash or behave abnormally
network_indicators: No direct network indicators from the vulnerability itself, but post-exploitation activity may include outbound connections from InDesign
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for crashes or abnormal behavior in Adobe InDesign when opening QXD files, especially those received from untrusted sources. Use endpoint protection or EDR solutions to detect exploitation attempts (e.g., memory corruption, shellcode execution). Employ IPS signatures targeting QXD file parsing anomalies and out-of-bounds memory access patterns. Analyze QXD files for malformed structures or fields that exceed expected sizes.
